catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class covers a device reset; cap.world.reset.v1 is for simulated worlds. The upstream reset writes '*RST' (drivers/SignalGenerator/KeysightN5182B.py:9-10) and takes no input and returns no output.

notes:
Checked on the fake backend only; no hardware was used and reviewed_by stays null. The fake reproduces the clone's KeysightN5182BMock state machine without importing or running the clone; the card preferred a transcript, but no recorded session was supplied, so the fake is a hand-written model of the upstream mock. The clone states no numeric frequency or power range (drivers/SignalGenerator/KeysightN5182B.py:12-16, 53-63), so both writes are Limit.operator_required: every write that sets them is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until site-limits.json supplies a bound. site-limits.example.json is an example operator overlay, not a device bound. The power value is in dBm; the SDK has no UCUM dBm atom, so the Field carries unit '1' and the description names dBm. NOT COVERED: the hardware path (host/port or VISA) was not run; no vendor datasheet in the clone states numeric limits; the transport-level set_timeout methods of SerialTransport and VisaTransport are transport options, not device capabilities, so they are not exposed as writes. The reset action uses x-cap.feifanphys.reset.v1 because no catalogue class fits a device reset. Licence recon: the clone README says MIT (README.md:202) but the clone has no LICENSE file; the lock keeps the task card's NOASSERTION and unknown license_class.
